confirmed_design_mismatches: Level 2 uses 90% static initial states and 10% walking handoffs; initial roll/pitch bounded at 8 degrees each, horizontal velocity components at 0.12 m/s. Broad recovery courses remain inaccessible behind quietness gates.

Level 2 learned exploration std 0.1581 to 0.2096, multiplied by 0.12 rad per action: approximately 1.09 to 1.44 degrees of independent per-control-step target noise. No entropy reward. This does not impose a hard limit on learned mean actions, but coherent large recovery sequences are exploration-rare.

Zero horizontal and angular velocity rewards apply during dynamic recovery as well as quiet standing. Phase weights mainly affect quiet pose bonus; they do not implement a different recovery learning objective.

Motion penalties have no discovery/refinement schedule, unlike official StandUp curricula. Actual action-rate and joint-velocity costs in the failed pre-fall windows are small, so they are not established as the dominant cause.
In 600-update failed trials the final 0.4 seconds still receive mean height reward 0.86 to 0.89 out of 1.0. Height alone is a poor tipping/recoverability signal in these traces.

Episode terminates at tilt above 55 degrees or root height below 60% nominal. Official StandUp permits recovery from ground configurations, whereas this experiment only covers pre-fall rescue and ends severe failures immediately. Ground rise is a separate behavior from the user's required prevention of falls.

failure_penalty.conclusion: Failure has a real penalty; increasing it alone cannot create recovery actions that were never sampled. Its appropriate magnitude requires comparing full discounted successful-recovery and failed-rollout returns.

failure_behavior.conclusion: Actor outputs change; there is no evidence of a frozen inference pipeline. Actual joint motion remains small and there is no coordinated effective rescue. Target changes do not prove a learned recovery.

official_lessons: Remove walking zero-velocity tracking from StandUp, use broad goal rewards and broad reset-state coverage.
Broad and sharp height rewards plus L1; upright rewards; upward-motion bootstrap below goal height; additional motion-blocking refinement costs introduced after recovery discovery.
Gaussian init std 1.0 with action scale 1.0: copy learning principles, not raw physical action or mechanical parameters, into XDuck.
next_work_before_any_new_training: Design mixed near-loss-of-balance, single-support, moving-handoff and quiet states in the same early curriculum.
Provide bounded coherent exploration on meaningful control timescales; verify PPO log probabilities against the actual sampled distribution and XDuck actuator limits.
Make restored balance and risk reduction primary during discovery; teach quiet settling and add stronger motion refinement afterwards while preserving mixed quiet samples.
Audit full discounted returns for successful dynamic rescue, rigid falling and perpetual motion before choosing failure penalties.

Require independent larger-perturbation tests to show nonfalling recovery and subsequent quietness; record new post-push steps and full-body target/actual responses. Do not reward step counts directly or require a prescribed rescue method.
limitations: These are verified configuration mismatches and measured behavior, not a causal ablation of each proposed root cause. Synthetic instantaneous reward probes are not feasible trajectories or proof of optimal policy.
